subtitle: Dolphin
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own setup guide requires "[Dolphin Gamecube/Wii Emulator]" and "Your EU ISO file, probably named `Mega Man X - Command Mission (Europe).iso`" -- a GameCube disc image.
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: the world's own archipelago.json: {"game": "Mega Man X: Command Mission"}, read 25 Aug 2026. ⚠ Note the colon -- the sheet lists this game as "Mega Man X Command Mission" without one, and the AP slot name is the world's spelling, not the sheet's.
description: Mega Man X: Command Mission as a multiworld. Characters, weapons, force metal and consumables are shuffled, with new Access Code and Rebellion Medal items gating the stages. Requires the player's own EU disc, Dolphin with MMU disabled, and the world's gclib folder installed into Archipelago's lib directory.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: GameCube title. The setup guide lists it among the player's own requirements: "Your EU ISO file".

rom.description: Your own Mega Man X: Command Mission disc image for GameCube -- the EUROPEAN (PAL) release, as an .iso file. The US version is not supported
rom._description_source: the setup guide, word for word: "Your EU ISO file, probably named `Mega Man X - Command Mission (Europe).iso`. Support for the US version is planned in the distant future." ⚠ Worth reading twice: this is one of the few worlds in the catalogue that wants the PAL disc and NOT the US one.
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. The guide states none.

emulator.name: Dolphin
emulator._source: the setup guide says to install Dolphin "making sure to install the most recent version" -- a direction, not a version number, so no minimum is recorded. The guide DOES state a hard setting: "Make sure Dolphin's MMU (Memory Management Unit) is disabled".

client.name: MMXCM Client
client._name_source: the world registers it under this exact name in worlds/commandmission/__init__.py: `Component("MMXCM Client", func=run_client, component_type=Type.CLIENT, ...)`. Its instructions page uses the same string: "the Mega Man X Command Mission client (MMXCM Client)".
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: worlds/commandmission/__init__.py does `Component("MMXCM Client", func=run_client, component_type=Type.CLIENT, ...)`, with the client itself in MMXCMClient.py/MMXCMContext.py. The world's own instructions make the order load-bearing: "You must open and connect the Mega Man X Command Mission client (MMXCM Client) to your Archipelago Server FIRST. Do this before opening Dolphin and the patched ISO each time you wish to play." London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/dolphin/extension.json declares {"protocol": "dolphin"} and DolphinBridge.Systems are ["GC", "Wii", "WII"]. The world reaches Dolphin itself -- its setup guide points at dolphin-memory-engine's own code-signing instructions for macOS, which is what its client uses to attach.
client._lua_note: No Lua. The world's client attaches to the running Dolphin process; there is no connector script to load.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest release read 25 Aug 2026 is V0.1.7, carrying commandmission.apworld, lib-windows.zip, lib-linux.zip and a sample YAML. ⚠ The apworld is NOT enough on its own -- see _manual_setup_note.
apworld._world_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"world_version": "0.1.4"}. ⚠ The newest release tag reads V0.1.7, so the world's own file and its tag disagree. Recorded as the world states it, with the difference visible.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"minimum_ap_version": "0.6.3"}. Our client is 0.6.7, so this is satisfied.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: the 9 .py files in worlds/commandmission were searched. __init__.py carries a patch_file_ending and MMXCMPatcher.py a result_file_ending, but NO `APPatchExtension` appears -- so there are no custom Python patch steps for London's patcher to refuse.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block. This world DOES produce a patched ISO, but Archipelago's own "Open Patch" does it and the world's client takes over from there -- the setup guide's troubleshooting is entirely about that flow. London neither builds nor applies it.

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.

_manual_setup_note: ⚠ THIS GAME NEEDS A SETUP STEP LONDON CANNOT DO. The setup guide requires the player to download lib-windows.zip (or lib-linux.zip) from the same release and extract its `gclib` folder into their Archipelago installation's /lib directory. Without it the world's client cannot reach Dolphin. London installs the apworld and starts the emulator; the gclib step, the MMU setting and the client-before-Dolphin order are the player's, and are named in `description`.
